claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first, user-owned portable context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge plus live resumable state—including evidence, decisions, plans, artifacts, unresolved questions, checkpoints, and next actions—with provenance and full-source access.

Cumulative cached replay represents continuity context reused across turns, whereas uncached input represents fresh per-case input; they must be reported separately, and cumulative replay must not be interpreted as a per-case token result or compared interchangeably with the BM25 mean. The frozen one-shot BM25 baseline passed 17/20 cases, recovered 48/53 evidence items, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens; it remains a regression fixture, not the target architecture.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned workspace transition path that reopens a parent checkpoint at revision N, refreshes to N+1 with an explicit evidence or constraint diff, batches typed query/read operations over exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, and commits an immutable child linked to its parent with preserved source references; it must avoid full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice.

The transition gate passes only when each case uses no more than four completed workspace calls, matches the direct-filesystem answer claims, verifies parent linkage, snapshot/revision pinning and source lineage, avoids full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice, and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.
